biology-2026-hl-q13a-scheme-nucleotide.alt: The scheme's model drawing of a DNA nucleotide: a circle labelled Phosphate joined to a pentagon labelled Deoxyribose, which is joined at another corner, at an angle, to a double ring of a hexagon and a pentagon labelled (Nitrogenous) base.

biology-2026-hl-q13b-ii-scheme.alt: The scheme's accepted forms of the heterozygous female genotype: XXNn, XNXn, X with N and X with n written as subscripts, and X with N and X with n written as superscripts.

No diaphragm and no ribs are drawn.

biology-2026-hl-q4-graphs.alt: Two line graphs side by side, each with Time on the horizontal axis. Graph 1, "Concentration of gas X", is a straight line rising steadily from a point part-way up the vertical axis. Graph 2, "Size of openings P", is a curve that starts high and falls, levelling off towards the right.

biology-2026-hl-q4-leaf-surface.alt: Light micrograph of the undersurface of a leaf: long, wavy-walled cells packed in rows, with five small lens-shaped pores scattered among them. Each pore is bordered by two curved cells, which a leader line labels Guard cells. Two arrows labelled P point to pores; two arrows labelled Q point to the ordinary surface cells between them.

biology-2026-hl-q5-translation.alt: Diagram of translation: a large grey blob labelled Structure A sits on a horizontal strand labelled mRNA, whose bases read A U G, G A G, C U G, C U A, G U A, A C A. Clover-shaped molecules carrying small balls dock on the strand by matching three-base sequences (U A C, C U C, G A C, G A U); an arrow labelled B points to one of them. The balls joined in a chain above are labelled Growing amino acid sequence.
biology-2026-hl-q5-translation.attribution: SEC Leaving Certificate Biology 2026 Higher Level examination paper — © State Examinations Commission; source credited in the paper's acknowledgements: biorender.com

biology-2026-hl-q6-nitrogen-cycle.alt: Flow diagram of the nitrogen cycle with boxes for Nitrogen gas, Nitrate, Plant biomolecules, Animal biomolecules, Urea, Molecule X and Molecule Y. A curved arrow A runs from Nitrogen gas to Nitrate. Nitrate leads to Plant biomolecules, and arrow B runs from Plant biomolecules to Animal biomolecules. Animal biomolecules, Urea and Plant biomolecules all lead to Molecule X; a curved arrow C runs from Molecule X up to Molecule Y and on, as C again, to Nitrate. No arrow leaves Nitrate or the molecules for Nitrogen gas.
biology-2026-hl-q6-nitrogen-cycle.attribution: SEC Leaving Certificate Biology 2026 Higher Level examination paper — © State Examinations Commission
